_transcription: ENGLISH PAGES: idx 2, 4, 6. The alternating hypothesis HELD with no exceptions, and every one of the 7 pages was opened and accounted for: idx 0 = bilingual cover (Series ABDC2/4, Set No. 3, Q.P. Code 65/4/3; 'this question paper contains 7 printed pages' and 'contains 14 questions'; 2 hours / 40 marks) | idx 1 = Hindi general instructions + खण्ड क + Q1-Q4 | idx 2 = English General Instructions + SECTION A + Q1-Q4 | idx 3 = Hindi Q5-Q10 | idx 4 = English Q5-Q10 | idx 5 = Hindi खण्ड ग + Q11-Q14 | idx 6 = English SECTION C + Q11-Q14. I read all three ODD pages AT FULL SIZE and NONE carries English overflow — each opens a fresh Hindi block (idx 1 'सामान्य निर्देश', idx 3 Hindi Q5, idx 5 'खण्ड ग') and each English block ends flush at a question boundary, so no question spans a language break. No parity inversion is possible here: the cover declares 7 printed pages, exactly 7 exist, and the last (idx 6, 'Page 7 of 7') is English. All 14 question numbers present and unbroken. STRUCTURE, off the printed General Instructions (idx 2): three sections, Section A Q1-6 @2 (12) + Section B Q7-10 @3 (12) + Section C Q11-14 @4 (16) = 40; instruction (vii) 'Question no. 14 is a case-study based question with 2 sub-parts of 2 marks each'. NO MCQs anywhere in the paper — all 19 rows are subjective, so there are no options, no answer letters, and no blind key re-derivation to run. INTERNAL CHOICE: instruction (vi) reads 'There is an internal choice in some questions' and prints NO COUNTS, so the count was established by walking the OFFICIAL MARKING SCHEME question by question (ms idx 2-9, which reprints every stem and both branches wherever an OR exists) and cross-reading the printed 'OR' on the paper itself. FOUR internal choices — Q1, Q9, Q10, Q13 — and TEN questions with none (Q2, Q3, Q4, Q5, Q6, Q7, Q8, Q11, Q12, Q14). Both branches ingested for all four. Row count 19 = 9 single + 4x2 alternatives + 1 case study x 2 sub-parts. Marking-scheme coverage verified complete: ms idx 0-1 are the evaluator's general instructions, idx 2-9 carry A1-A14 with no question missing. Note the marks sum cannot prove the OR count (a dropped alternative costs a row without moving the total), which is exactly why the scheme was walked. OVERLAP WITH 65/4/1, measured by CONTENT rather than by plan.txt: 15 of the 19 rows are the same question as a 65/4/1 row. For each I confirmed the match on MY OWN page and then reused the reference file's stem/context text BYTE-FOR-BYTE, so the row dedups at commit while the sitting stays reconstructable. Mapping (this paper -> 65/4/1): Q1a->Q4a, Q1b->Q4b, Q2->Q6, Q4->Q2, Q5->Q3, Q6->Q5, Q9a->Q10a, Q9b->Q10b, Q10a->Q8a, Q10b->Q8b, Q12->Q11, Q13a->Q12a, Q13b->Q12b, Q14a->Q14a, Q14b->Q14b. GENUINELY NEW (4 rows): Q3 (three friends' photograph — conditional probability), Q7 (area between y=mx and x^2=y equals 32/3, find m), Q8 (projection of c+lambda*b on a is 2*sqrt(6), find lambda), Q11 (definite integral of x^4/(1+e^x) over -3 to 3). PLAN.TXT WAS WRONG IN BOTH DIRECTIONS, exactly as warned. It claimed 7 blocks covered / 5 new; the measured truth is 15 rows shared / 4 new. It told me to SKIP Q3 as '65-4-1 Q1' — false, 65/4/1's Q1 is the bag of 3 red and 4 white balls while this Q3 is the photograph question and is NEW; and to SKIP Q8 as '65-4-1 Q9' — false, 65/4/1's Q9 is the mutually-perpendicular-vectors proof while this Q8 is the projection/lambda question and is NEW. Conversely it listed Q2 under TRANSCRIBE when Q2 IS 65/4/1's Q6 verbatim. Two of its remaining skips point at the right CONTENT under the wrong reference number (its 'Q9 = 65-4-1 Q6#2' and 'Q13 = 65-4-1 Q13#1' are really 65/4/1's Q10 and Q12). Only Q4->Q2, Q6->Q5 and Q12->Q11 were right on both content and number. TAXONOMY: Q5 and Q12 are plane questions and are filed on Three Dimensional Geometry / The Plane, the 2026-08-19 subtopic; Q4 uses Probability / Random Variables and Probability Distributions. PRINTING NOTE (no row flag, nothing turns on it): Q8's stem strings two clauses with a doubled conjunction — 'b = i + j - 2k and c = i + 3j - k and the projection of vector...' — where a comma before 'and c' is clearly meant. Transcribed as printed; the official marking scheme (ms idx 4) reprints it identically, so it is CBSE's own typesetting rather than a render artefact. The same is true of the archery passage's 'is likely the earn' (see the flag on Q14a).

questions.stem: If \(|\vec{a} \times \vec{b}|^2 + |\vec{a} \cdot \vec{b}|^2 = 400\) and \(|\vec{b}| = 5\), then find the value of \(|\vec{a}|\).
Find all the possible vectors of magnitude \(5\sqrt{3}\) which are equally inclined to the coordinate axes.
Three friends A, B and C got their photograph clicked. Find the probability that B is standing at the central position, given that A is standing at the left corner.

A coin is tossed twice. The following table shows the probability distribution of number of tails :

| X | 0 | 1 | 2 |
|---|---|---|---|
| P(X) | K | 6K | 9K |

(a) Find the value of K.

(b) Is the coin tossed biased or unbiased ? Justify your answer.
The foot of a perpendicular drawn from the point \((-2, -1, -3)\) on a plane is \((1, -3, 3)\). Find the equation of the plane.

Find the general solution of the differential equation

\(\sec^2 x \cdot \tan y \, dx + \sec^2 y \cdot \tan x \, dy = 0.\)

questions.subtopic: Area Bounded by a Curve and a Line
questions.stem: If the area of the region bounded by the line \(y = mx\) and the curve \(x^2 = y\) is \(\dfrac{32}{3}\) sq. units, then find the positive value of m, using integration.

If \(\vec{a} = 2\hat{i} - \hat{j} + \hat{k}\), \(\vec{b} = \hat{i} + \hat{j} - 2\hat{k}\) and \(\vec{c} = \hat{i} + 3\hat{j} - \hat{k}\) and the projection of vector \(\vec{c} + \lambda \vec{b}\) on vector \(\vec{a}\) is \(2\sqrt{6}\), then find the value of \(\lambda\).

If a line makes \(60^\circ\) and \(45^\circ\) angles with the positive directions of x-axis and z-axis respectively, then find the angle that it makes with the positive direction of y-axis. Hence, write the direction cosines of the line.
questions._flag: OFFICIAL KEY IS INCOMPLETE (not wrong) — a finding for the solution-authoring step, not something to resolve here. The marking scheme correctly derives \(m^2 = 1/4 \Rightarrow m = \pm 1/2\) and then reports only \(\theta = 60^\circ\) with direction cosines \(\langle 1/2, 1/2, 1/\sqrt{2} \rangle\), silently dropping the \(m = -1/2\) branch (angle \(120^\circ\), direction cosines \(\langle 1/2, -1/2, 1/\sqrt{2} \rangle\)), which the printed stem admits just as much. Marking scheme page idx 5. Independently observed on 65/4/1 Q10(a), which is the same question with the same marking-scheme block, so this is a series-wide key omission rather than a one-off.

questions.stem: Check whether the lines \(\dfrac{x - 1}{2} = \dfrac{y - 2}{3} = \dfrac{z - 3}{4}\) and \(\dfrac{x - 4}{5} = \dfrac{y - 1}{2} = z\) are skew or not.

questions.subtopic: Definite Integrals and the Fundamental Theorem

questions.stem: Find the equations of the planes passing through the line of intersection of the planes \(\vec{r} \cdot (\hat{i} + 3\hat{j}) = 6\) and \(\vec{r} \cdot (3\hat{i} - \hat{j} - 4\hat{k}) = 0\), which are at a distance of 1 unit from the origin.
Find the particular solution of the differential equation \(x \dfrac{dy}{dx} + y + \dfrac{1}{1 + x^2} = 0\), given that \(y(1) = 0\).

Find the general solution of the differential equation

\(x (y^3 + x^3) \, dy = (2y^4 + 5x^3 y) \, dx.\)

questions.context:
In a game of Archery, each ring of the Archery target is valued. The centremost ring is worth 10 points and rest of the rings are allotted points 9 to 1 in sequential order moving outwards.

Archer A is likely to earn 10 points with a probability of \(0{\cdot}8\) and Archer B is likely the earn 10 points with a probability of \(0{\cdot}9\).

Based on the above information, answer the following questions :

If both of them hit the Archery target, then find the probability that
questions.stem: exactly one of them earns 10 points.
questions._figure: DECORATIVE — the printed archery-target illustration (page idx 6) only labels the rings '1 point' to '10 points', which the passage already states in words. Both probabilities needed (0·8, 0·9) are in the stem text. Not attached.
questions._flag: PRINTED AS-IS: the passage reads 'Archer B is likely the earn 10 points' where 'to earn' is meant. Transcribed faithfully. This is CBSE's own typesetting error, not a render artefact — the official marking scheme (page idx 8) reprints the passage with the identical wording, as does 65/4/1.
